data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by the Kubernetes readiness probe configuration. The application completed its initialisation in approximately 6.1 seconds, but the pod was not marked as Ready for another 18.9 seconds due to the initialDelaySeconds setting. This configuration caused the total startup time to exceed the 10-second SLO.

findings.statement: The application completed its startup sequence in 6.113 seconds, as confirmed by logs and span data.
The readiness probe configuration includes an initialDelaySeconds of 20 seconds, which accounts for the 18.887-second delay before the pod was marked Ready.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull duration was only 4.552 seconds for a 53 MB image, which is efficient.
Application initialisation was fast, taking only 1.013 seconds.
Scheduling duration was 0.0 seconds, indicating no resource contention or scheduling delays.

recommendations.action: Reduce initialDelaySeconds in the readiness probe configuration.
recommendations.rationale: The current 20-second delay is significantly longer than the actual application startup time of approximately 6 seconds, causing unnecessary latency.
A startup probe would allow the application to signal readiness as soon as it is finished, while keeping the readiness probe for ongoing health checks.
